documents.title: Delay in the Greenfield Medical Center project
documents.text:
To: Project Steering Committee
From: Nadia Petrenko, Project Manager
Subject: Revised timeline for the Greenfield Medical Center

Dear colleagues,

I am writing to update you on the status of the Greenfield Medical Center. As you know, the building was due to be handed over on 15 September. Unfortunately, the supplier of the imaging equipment has informed us that a shipment of components has been held up, and installation of the two scanners cannot begin until the end of October. [A] Since the scanners are the largest fixtures in the building, we cannot certify the radiology wing as ready until they have been tested.

Rather than delay the whole opening, I propose a staged approach. The outpatient clinic, laboratory and pharmacy, which do not depend on the scanners, would open as planned in mid-September. [B] Radiology would follow in the first week of December, after a two-week period of calibration. This would mean that patients needing scans would continue to be referred to the Marlowe Hospital for a further eleven weeks, at a cost to us of approximately 4,200 dollars per week. [C]

I recognize that the extra expense is not negligible, but a full postponement would mean paying staff who could not yet see patients. I would be grateful if you could indicate your preference by Friday so that we can inform the health authority before its next review. [D]

Regards,
Nadia

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the e-mail?
choices: To report that the building has been damaged
To suggest a way of dealing with a late delivery
To request a larger budget for new scanners
To announce the replacement of a supplier
questions.explanation: Ms. Petrenko explains a delayed shipment and proposes a staged opening. The building is not damaged, no budget increase is requested, and no supplier is replaced.

choices: The health authority must complete its review
The staff must finish a period of training
The pharmacy must receive its final license
The imaging machines must be installed and tested
questions.explanation: She says the wing cannot be certified until the scanners have been tested.

questions.prompt: What would be the approximate additional cost of referring patients elsewhere?
choices: About 46,000 dollars
About 4,200 dollars
About 8,400 dollars
About 460,000 dollars
questions.explanation: Eleven weeks at approximately 4,200 dollars per week comes to about 46,200 dollars.

questions.prompt: In which position marked [A], [B], [C] or [D] does the following sentence best belong? "Together, these services are expected to account for about two thirds of the center's patient visits."
questions.explanation: 'These services' refers to the clinic, laboratory and pharmacy mentioned just before [B]. At [A], [C] and [D] the sentence would have no clear referent.

documents.title: Library cards for the digital age
documents.text:
Public libraries have long been measured by the number of books they lend, but a growing group of librarians argue that this figure no longer captures what a library does. In the city of Wexford, where physical loans have fallen by a fifth in five years, the library service has quietly become one of the busiest providers of digital skills training in the county.

Under a program launched two years ago, residents can book one-hour sessions with a staff member to learn anything from setting up an e-mail account to filing a tax return online. Demand has been strongest among people over sixty and among newly arrived immigrants, many of whom, according to head librarian Joanna Kessler, "come in for help with a single form and stay to join a conversation group." The sessions are free, although some courses, such as spreadsheet skills, require a modest materials fee.

Not all council members are persuaded. Councillor Alan Pryce has questioned whether the library should be using public funds for services that private colleges also provide. Ms. Kessler responds that private courses are priced beyond the reach of those who need them most. An independent evaluation, due next March, will examine whether participants go on to find work or to use public services online more confidently. Until then, the library has hired two additional trainers and extended opening hours on Thursdays.

questions.prompt: What is the article mainly about?
choices: The decline of reading among local residents
A dispute between libraries and private colleges
A library's expanding role beyond lending books
A national plan to modernize public buildings
questions.explanation: The article describes how Wexford's library has become a provider of digital skills training as lending falls. The dispute with colleges is a secondary point.

questions.prompt: Who has used the training sessions most?
choices: Students who need help with their schoolwork
Staff members of the county council offices
Older residents and recent arrivals in the country
Local business owners who file tax returns
questions.explanation: Demand has been strongest among people over sixty and among newly arrived immigrants.

questions.prompt: What is Councillor Pryce's concern?
choices: Public money may be spent on a service offered elsewhere
Library staff are not qualified as teachers
The library is open for too few hours on Thursdays
Participants are not given enough support to find jobs
questions.explanation: He questions whether public funds should be used for services private colleges also provide.

questions.prompt: What will the evaluation next March look at?
choices: How many books are borrowed by older residents
Whether the new trainers are paid at the correct rate
Which courses should carry a materials fee
Whether trainees later find jobs or use online services
questions.explanation: It will examine whether participants go on to find work or to use public services online more confidently.

documents.title: Messages between Imani Okoye and Felix Brandt
documents.text:
Imani Okoye (2:41 p.m.): Felix, the client just called. They want to move tomorrow's site visit to Thursday because their engineer is stuck at the airport. Are you free then?
Felix Brandt (2:44 p.m.): Thursday morning is fine, but I have the safety audit at Dockside after lunch. How long will the visit take?
Imani Okoye (2:46 p.m.): About three hours with the walk-through, so we'd finish before one if we start at nine. I'd drive, since the train times are awkward.
Felix Brandt (2:48 p.m.): Great. Could you ask them to send the floor plans in advance? Last time we only received them on arrival and we lost half an hour.
Imani Okoye (2:50 p.m.): Already asked. They said the plans are being updated because of the new loading bay, so we'll get the revised version tonight.
Felix Brandt (2:52 p.m.): Perfect. In that case I'll prepare the cost estimate for the extension, so we can present figures on the day rather than send them afterward.
Imani Okoye (2:53 p.m.): That would impress them. I'll book the meeting room for the debrief, just in case it runs over.

documents.title: Corvallis Savings: Home improvement loans
documents.text:
Planning a renovation? A Corvallis home improvement loan lets you borrow between 5,000 and 60,000 dollars at a fixed rate, with repayment terms of up to ten years. The rate depends on the amount and duration: loans under 15,000 dollars carry a rate of 6.9 percent, while larger loans are offered at 5.8 percent. There are no fees for setting up the loan or for early repayment.

Eligibility: applicants must be over eighteen, have been employed or self-employed for at least twelve months, and own the property to be improved. Work financed by the loan must be carried out by a registered contractor; do-it-yourself projects are not eligible. Applicants must provide a written quote from the contractor with their form.

How it works: after approval, which normally takes three working days, the funds are paid directly to the contractor in two installments, the first before work begins and the second once our inspector confirms completion. Customers who also hold a Corvallis current account for more than one year benefit from a rate reduction of 0.4 percentage points. To apply, complete the online form or visit any branch with proof of income and a copy of the property deed.

documents.title: Question about renovation financing
documents.text:
Dear Corvallis Savings,

I own an apartment in Lakeview and plan to replace the kitchen and flooring for about 18,000 dollars. I have been your current account customer for three years and I have been employed by the same firm for eight months, although I was self-employed before that for four years. I intend to hire a contractor for the plumbing but to install the tiles myself to save money. Could you tell me whether I am eligible and what rate I would receive?

Thank you,
Grace Lindqvist

documents.title: Re: Question about renovation financing
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Lindqvist,

Thank you for your interest. Your employment history meets our twelve-month requirement, since we count self-employment too. Please note, however, that the loan can cover only the part of the project carried out by a registered professional, so the tiling you plan to do yourself would have to be funded another way. A written quote for the plumbing and the kitchen units installed by the contractor is all we need.

On the basis of the amount you would borrow, the standard rate would apply, with the reduction for your account. I have attached the application form.

Sincerely,
Noor Rahman, Loans Advisor

choices: To complain about the interest rate she was charged
To close her current account with the bank
To find out whether she can obtain financing for a project
To ask for a contractor to be recommended
questions.explanation: She describes her project and asks whether she is eligible and what rate she would receive.

documents.title: Quality Assurance Technician: Orwell Medical Devices
documents.text:
Orwell Medical Devices, a manufacturer of surgical instruments employing 340 people, is hiring a Quality Assurance Technician for its Leeds plant. You will inspect components at each stage of production, document any defects and work with engineers to trace their causes. The role is based on the production floor, and you will be required to wear protective clothing throughout your shift.

You should have a technical diploma and at least two years of experience in a regulated manufacturing environment, preferably medical or aerospace. Familiarity with ISO 13485 is a strong advantage. Attention to detail and clear written communication are essential, since your reports will be reviewed by external auditors.

We offer a salary between 31,000 and 36,000 pounds, depending on experience, private health insurance after six months, and funding toward a professional qualification. The position involves rotating shifts, including every third weekend. To apply, send your résumé to careers@orwellmed.example, quoting reference QA-14, by 12 May. We particularly welcome applications from candidates who have experience of electronic recording systems.

documents.title: Application, reference QA-14
documents.text:
Dear Hiring Team,

Please find enclosed my résumé for the Quality Assurance Technician position. I have worked for three years at Kestrel Aerospace in Bristol, where I inspect machined parts and maintain the inspection database. My duties include writing nonconformance reports that are reviewed by customers' auditors, and I recently helped trace a recurring surface defect to a worn cutting tool, which saved the company an estimated 40,000 pounds.

I do not yet hold ISO 13485 certification, but my employer has agreed to sponsor me for the course in June. I hold a national diploma in engineering technology. My main concern is the rotating weekend shifts, as I am a carer for a relative on alternate Saturdays; I would be grateful if you could tell me whether a fixed weekend arrangement might be possible.

Yours faithfully,
Daniel Achebe

documents.title: Letter from Dunmore Community College
documents.text:
Dear Mr. Singh,

Thank you for your inquiry about the part-time Certificate in Project Management. I am writing to confirm several details. The program consists of eight evening modules, each lasting five weeks, and can be completed in about eighteen months. The fee is 2,400 dollars, which may be paid in three installments; a discount of ten percent applies to those who enroll before 1 August.

Applicants do not need a university degree, but they must have at least two years of work experience, which can be in any sector. Candidates who have previously studied project management may apply for exemption from the first module by submitting their transcript, although exemption does not reduce the fee.

Classes are held on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, from 6:30 to 9:00. Because the college is adjacent to Dunmore Station, many students arrive directly from work; a light meal is available in the cafeteria until 6:15. To reserve your place, please return the enclosed form together with a deposit of 300 dollars, which will be deducted from the final installment.

Sincerely,
Marguerite Alder, Admissions Office

documents.title: Message from Rohan Singh to a colleague
documents.text: Just got the college's letter. The course is more expensive than the one at Harmon Institute, but it's evenings only, which suits my schedule. If I sign up before August I'd save a bit. I did a short course in project planning in 2021 so I might skip the first part. Could you check whether our manager would contribute? Last year they covered half of Kamal's tuition. If it works out, I would also like to ask whether the company could let me leave the office early on Tuesdays and Thursdays so that I can reach the college on time, and I could make up the hours on Friday afternoons or at the weekend, whichever suits the team better.

documents.title: Public notice: Proposed changes to bus route 14
documents.text:
The Marlow Transit Authority proposes to modify bus route 14, which currently connects the Riverside district with the university campus via Market Street. Under the proposal, which would take effect on 6 January, the route would be shortened to end at the Central Library, while a new route 14X would run express between Riverside and the campus, stopping only at the hospital.

The authority believes the changes would reduce journey times for most passengers by about eight minutes. Passengers who currently board at stops along Market Street would be served by route 22, whose frequency would increase to every ten minutes at peak hours. However, the authority acknowledges that some riders with limited mobility would face a longer walk to the nearest stop.

The public is invited to comment in three ways: at the open meeting on 2 December in the council chamber, by e-mail to routes@marlowtransit.example, or by post to the address below. All comments received by 15 December will be reviewed by the board, which will announce its decision on 20 December. A final vote is not guaranteed to follow the proposal as written; the board may adopt it in modified form or reject it altogether.

questions.prompt: What is the notice mainly about?
choices: A suggested alteration to a transit service
A reduction in the price of bus fares
The opening of a new university campus
The closing of a hospital stop
questions.explanation: The notice describes a proposed change to route 14 and invites comments. Fares, campus openings and hospital closures are not mentioned.

questions.prompt: What would happen to people who now board on Market Street?
choices: They would have to walk to the Central Library
They would use the new express service
They would be transferred to a different route
They would no longer have any bus service
questions.explanation: They would be served by route 22, with greater frequency at peak hours.

questions.prompt: What is suggested about the proposal?
choices: It was approved before the notice was published
It will start on the same day as the final vote
It could be changed after the public has given views
It is intended to reduce the number of riders
questions.explanation: The board may adopt it in modified form or reject it after reviewing the comments, so it is not final.

questions.prompt: Which person would be most disadvantaged by the proposal?
choices: A traveler who has difficulty walking far
A student who commutes to the campus every day
A patient who travels to the hospital by bus
A worker who lives in the Riverside district
questions.explanation: The authority says riders with limited mobility would face a longer walk to the nearest stop; the others would gain faster journeys.
